subject: FIND-STRING function
notes: EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED, verdict unchanged (kb/Work PB254). Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.37.4 "argument-3 represents the number of matches to ignore" -> OK (15.37.4 rule 2); --check 15.37.3 "argument-3 shall be an integer data item or integer literal" -> OK (15.37.3 rule 3). r3 places NO constraint on argument-3's value, so rule 2 has to answer for EVERY integer, and this row was CONFORMS with its widest half unmeasured: find_string_skip_domain stops at PIC 9(18) VALUE 999999999999999999, one order of magnitude BELOW long.MaxValue, which is exactly where the defect lived. FIXED by giving FindString's skip parameter the Int128 carrier and the renderer arm the wide intake (IntArgWide), the declared-carrier pairing that IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests.EveryTotalIntegerArgument_TakesTheWideIntake now holds. kb/Work R08 had already removed an (int) narrowing INSIDE this body and left the Int128->long one at the intake - the same rule, one level up. conformance:cases/15.37.4-Returned-value-rules/find_string now carries EXHAUST3 (the in-range boundary: three matches, ignore three, none left), WIDESKIP (a 19-digit literal) and WIDELASTSKIP (a PIC 9(19) item under LAST), all 0.
